config.title: Feature Flag Hook

intro.title: Feature Flag Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Angular service that acts as a 'feature flag hook' to control the visibility of UI features in your application. You will learn how to use Angular's dependency injection and RxJS Observables to create a centralized flag management system. The core concept involves conditionally rendering components based on boolean flags fetched from a mock configuration. By the end, you'll have a service that can be injected anywhere to toggle features on or off dynamically.
intro.usecase: Feature flags are essential for controlled rollouts in production applications. In Angular dashboards, they allow teams to gradually enable new analytics panels or experimental data visualizations for specific user segments. E-commerce platforms use feature flags to test checkout flow improvements or seasonal promotions with limited audiences before full deployment. This pattern also enables A/B testing of UI components like redesigned navigation menus or updated form layouts while maintaining a stable user experience for most customers.

objectives: Construct a custom Angular service to manage feature flag state
Implement a reactive feature flag hook using Angular's dependency injection
Configure component templates to conditionally render content based on feature flags
Integrate the feature flag service into multiple components within an Angular application
Manipulate feature flag values dynamically to control UI visibility
Initialize feature flags with default values and update them through user interactions
Bind component logic to feature flag changes using Angular's change detection

steps.title: Import Component and Injectable from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component and Injectable from '@angular/core' at the top of your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to bring in multiple symbols from the same module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Angular core decorators
import { Component, Injectable } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports for creating Angular components and injectable services.
successCriteria: Component and Injectable are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Component and Injectable from Angular core. These are essential decorators for creating components and services in Angular.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Component and Injectable from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please import both Component and Injectable from the '@angular/core' module using the correct import syntax.

steps.title: Create FeatureFlagService with Injectable decorator
steps.instruction: Create a class named FeatureFlagService and decorate it with @Injectable() to make it an Angular service.
steps.hint: Use the @Injectable() decorator above your class definition. The class should be exportable.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, Injectable } from '@angular/core';

// Create FeatureFlagService class with @Injectable() decorator
steps.expectedOutcome: A FeatureFlagService class is defined with the @Injectable() decorator, ready to be used as an injectable service.
successCriteria: FeatureFlagService class is created and decorated with @Injectable().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an injectable service. This service can now be provided and injected into components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the @Injectable() decorator and the FeatureFlagService class definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The service wasn't created correctly. Check that you used @Injectable() and defined the FeatureFlagService class.

steps.title: Add feature flags object to FeatureFlagService
steps.instruction: Inside the FeatureFlagService class, add a private property named 'featureFlags' with type Record<string, boolean> and initialize it with an object containing at least two feature flags (e.g., 'newDashboard' and 'darkMode') set to boolean values.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript's Record type to define an object with string keys and boolean values. Initialize it directly in the property declaration.
steps.expectedOutcome: The FeatureFlagService will have a private featureFlags property storing configuration for feature flags.
successCriteria: FeatureFlagService contains a private 'featureFlags' property of type Record<string, boolean> initialized with at least two feature flag entries.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the feature flags configuration object to your service.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the property is private, has the correct Record<string, boolean> type, and is initialized with an object containing boolean values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The feature flags property is missing or incorrect. Check the property name, type, and initialization syntax.

steps.title: Create isEnabled method in FeatureFlagService
steps.instruction: Inside the FeatureFlagService class, add a public method named isEnabled that takes a flagName parameter of type string and returns a boolean.
steps.hint: Remember to use TypeScript type annotations for the parameter and return type. The method should be public so it can be called from other components.
steps.expectedOutcome: The FeatureFlagService will have a public method that can be used to check if a specific feature flag is enabled.
successCriteria: The FeatureFlagService contains a public isEnabled method with a string parameter and boolean return type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the isEnabled method to your FeatureFlagService. This method will serve as the main API for checking feature flag status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your method is public, has the correct parameter type (string), and returns a boolean value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isEnabled method is missing or doesn't match the required signature. Check that you've added a public method with a string parameter and boolean return type.

steps.title: Create FeatureFlagComponent with Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component class named FeatureFlagComponent and decorate it with @Component().
steps.hint: Add a class declaration with the @Component decorator from '@angular/core'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A FeatureFlagComponent class is created with the @Component decorator applied.
successCriteria: The FeatureFlagComponent class exists and is decorated with @Component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the FeatureFlagComponent with the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a class named FeatureFlagComponent and applied the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FeatureFlagComponent with @Component decorator wasn't created correctly. Check the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Add FeatureFlagService to component constructor
steps.instruction: In the FeatureFlagComponent class, add a constructor that injects FeatureFlagService as a private parameter.
steps.hint: Use the constructor keyword with a parameter of type FeatureFlagService, and mark it as private to make it a class property.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: injecting a service
constructor(private dataService: DataService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The FeatureFlagComponent now has a constructor that receives FeatureFlagService via dependency injection.
successCriteria: FeatureFlagComponent has a constructor with a private parameter of type FeatureFlagService.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully injected FeatureFlagService into your component using Angular's dependency injection.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the constructor parameter is typed as FeatureFlagService and marked as private.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a constructor to FeatureFlagComponent with a private FeatureFlagService parameter.

steps.title: Create component properties for feature flags
steps.instruction: Inside the FeatureFlagComponent class, add two public properties: 'showNewFeature' and 'showBetaFeature', both typed as boolean and initialized to false.
steps.hint: Add these properties directly in the class body, using TypeScript syntax: propertyName: type = initialValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The FeatureFlagComponent will have two boolean properties to track feature flag states.
successCriteria: The FeatureFlagComponent class contains 'showNewFeature: boolean = false' and 'showBetaFeature: boolean = false' as public properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the feature flag state properties to your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some properties, but make sure both 'showNewFeature' and 'showBetaFeature' are present with boolean types and false initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component properties are missing or incorrect. Add two public boolean properties initialized to false.

steps.title: Initialize feature flag properties in ngOnInit
steps.instruction: Implement the ngOnInit lifecycle hook in your FeatureFlagComponent to initialize the feature flag properties using the service's isEnabled method.
steps.hint: Add ngOnInit method inside the component class and set each property to the result of calling this.featureFlagService.isEnabled() with the appropriate flag name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an ngOnInit method that initializes all three feature flag properties using the service.
successCriteria: ngOnInit method is implemented and sets newDashboardEnabled, darkModeEnabled, and exportFeatureEnabled using featureFlagService.isEnabled()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the ngOnInit lifecycle hook to initialize your feature flag properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added ngOnInit, but make sure you're initializing all three feature flag properties using the service's isEnabled method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method is missing or not properly implemented. Try adding the ngOnInit lifecycle hook and initializing the feature flag properties.

steps.title: Add template with feature flag conditional display
steps.instruction: In the FeatureFlagComponent's template, add a paragraph element that displays 'New Dashboard is enabled!' only when the newDashboardEnabled property is true, using Angular's *ngIf directive.
steps.hint: Use the *ngIf structural directive with the component property to conditionally show content. The syntax is *ngIf="propertyName".
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will conditionally display content based on the newDashboardEnabled feature flag property.
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph element with *ngIf directive that uses the newDashboardEnabled property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional display using Angular's *ngIf directive.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the *ngIf directive with the correct property name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required conditional display. Try adding a paragraph with *ngIf="newDashboardEnabled".

steps.title: Add toggle button to the template
steps.instruction: In the FeatureFlagComponent template, add a button element with the text 'Toggle Dark Mode' that will be used to toggle the darkModeEnabled flag.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element inside the template string. The button text should be 'Toggle Dark Mode'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The FeatureFlagComponent template now contains a button element with the text 'Toggle Dark Mode'.
successCriteria: The template includes a <button> element with the text content 'Toggle Dark Mode'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a toggle button to the template. This button will be used to toggle the dark mode feature flag.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the button has the exact text 'Toggle Dark Mode' and is properly placed in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required button element. Please add a <button> with the text 'Toggle Dark Mode' to the template.

steps.title: Create toggle method in component
steps.instruction: In the FeatureFlagComponent class, add a method named toggleFeatureFlag that takes a flagName parameter of type string and toggles the corresponding feature flag property.
steps.hint: Create a method that updates the boolean value of the matching property (like newDashboardEnabled) to its opposite value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can toggle the state of individual feature flags when called.
successCriteria: The FeatureFlagComponent class contains a toggleFeatureFlag method that accepts a string parameter and toggles the corresponding boolean property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the toggle method that will allow users to toggle feature flags.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it properly toggles the boolean value of the matching feature flag property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleFeatureFlag method is missing or doesn't properly toggle the feature flag properties. Review the method implementation.

steps.title: Wire toggle button to toggle method
steps.instruction: In the FeatureFlagComponent template, add a (click) event binding to the button that calls the toggleFeatureFlag method with the appropriate feature flag name.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="methodName(argument)" on the button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button click to a method
<button (click)="handleClick('someValue')">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button in the template will be connected to the toggleFeatureFlag method via a click event binding.
successCriteria: The button element has a (click) event binding that calls toggleFeatureFlag with a feature flag name argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the button click to the toggle method. The feature flag can now be toggled interactively.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the event binding might be incomplete. Make sure you're using (click)="toggleFeatureFlag('featureName')" syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly connected to the toggle method. Remember to use Angular's (click) event binding syntax.
